Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
12 October 2026 .
Brent $ 106.75 + 1.94 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 CNN reports a tanker was hit in the Strait of Hormuz area, in the most recent development from this feed.

02 Brent stood at $106.75 as of 15:12 UTC, up 1.94% over 24 hours; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

03 Iran is still reviewing a US response on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and will reply via intermediaries when ready, foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said, per MarineLink.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with tanker strikes continuing. CNN reports a tanker was hit in the strait area; this is the lead development in this feed window. Separately, the IRGC has claimed strikes on supertankers in recent days, including claims relayed by Anadolu Agency citing Iranian state media that a third tanker was hit, and Breakingthenews.net also carries the IRGC claim of a tanker strike. Two merchant vessels carrying 22 Indian crew were attacked in the strait, with two seafarers missing, per Telegraph India and ThePrint; this was reported in an earlier feed window and is not a new development. On the diplomatic track, MarineLink reports that Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Iran is still reviewing a US response to its strait-reopening proposal and will reply via intermediaries when the review is complete, leaving any Iran-US channel stalled. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $106.75 as of 15:12 UTC, a gain of 1.94% over 24 hours. This feed indexed 87 headlines in the last 24 hours. As of 15:20 UTC, 141 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
